trunk-motor.name: Tummy and back muscles that have switched off
trunk-motor.explanation: Your symptoms sit in the trunk muscles rather than the spine itself. Breathing, gentle bracing and steady loading usually settle it.
trunk-motor.course: Often improves within a few weeks once the trunk muscles are used consistently rather than hard.
trunk-motor.helps: Short, frequent sessions. Stop before form breaks down, not when it hurts.

shoulder-instability.name: A shoulder that feels insecure
shoulder-instability.explanation: After a sprain or a dislocation the shoulder often feels loose or guards itself. We build steadiness in the arc where you feel safe.
shoulder-instability.course: Confidence in the shoulder usually returns gradually over 6–12 weeks of steady loading.
shoulder-instability.helps: Keep the arm in front of you at first. Avoid end-range external rotation with load.

scapular.name: Pain around the shoulder blade
scapular.explanation: The blade has to glide for the arm to work. When it sticks, the shoulder and neck both take the load.
scapular.course: Responds well to a few weeks of controlled movement and loading.
scapular.helps: Move the blade, then load it. Posture cues alone rarely fix this.

itb.name: Pain on the outside of the knee or thigh
itb.explanation: The band down the outside of the thigh gets loaded heavily when the hip muscles do less work. It settles with hip strength and a temporary reduction in volume.
itb.course: Usually improves over 4–8 weeks when running or walking load is cut back and rebuilt.
itb.helps: Reduce distance first, then strengthen the hip. Stretching the band itself changes little.

hamstring-strain.name: Back of the thigh, sore when you push off
hamstring-strain.explanation: The hamstring is usually irritated at its muscle belly or near the sit bone. It heals best under gradual load, not rest and stretching.
hamstring-strain.course: Expect 3–6 weeks for a simple strain; heavier ones take longer.
hamstring-strain.helps: Isometrics early, slow lengthening under load later. Avoid aggressive stretching for a week.

thigh-muscle.name: Thigh muscle ache after activity
thigh-muscle.explanation: Front, side or back of the thigh, usually reproduced by the same contraction that hurt it. Capacity, not damage, is the limiting factor.
thigh-muscle.course: Typically settles in 2–4 weeks with steady loading.
thigh-muscle.helps: Keep the muscle working through the range that does not sharp-pain.

gluteal-tendon.name: Pain on the outside of your hip
gluteal-tendon.explanation: The gluteal tendons sit over the bony point of the hip. They dislike compression — lying on that side and long strides — as much as they dislike load.
gluteal-tendon.course: Slow but reliable: 8–12 weeks is common for tendon symptoms.
gluteal-tendon.helps: Sleep with a pillow between the knees, avoid crossing legs, load it steadily.

groin-strain.name: Groin that pulls when you push off
groin-strain.explanation: The adductor muscles are usually overloaded rather than torn. They respond to gradual loading across the whole range.
groin-strain.course: 4–8 weeks for a simple strain; longer if load is returned too fast.
groin-strain.helps: Squeeze exercises early, then change-of-direction work late.

hip-flexor.name: Pinching at the front of the hip
hip-flexor.explanation: A pinch at a fixed angle is usually the soft tissues being compressed, not damage. Working around the pinch keeps things moving.
hip-flexor.course: Settles over a few weeks when the provocative angle is respected.
hip-flexor.helps: Stop short of the pinch, then extend the range weekly.

ankle-instability.name: An ankle that keeps going over
ankle-instability.explanation: After repeated sprains the ankle reacts more slowly than it needs to. Balance and peroneal work is the treatment.
ankle-instability.course: Neuromuscular gains build over 6–8 weeks of short daily practice.
ankle-instability.helps: Practice balance on soft surfaces, progress to turning and landing.

shin-stress.name: Shin pain that builds with impact
shin-stress.explanation: Pain along the inner shin that worsens with running is a load-tolerance problem. Bone stress needs load removed early, not pushed through.
shin-stress.course: A few weeks of reduced impact plus calf and hip capacity usually settles it.
shin-stress.helps: Reduce impact now, keep non-impact fitness, rebuild distance slowly.

forefoot.name: Ball of the foot or toes
forefoot.explanation: Forefoot pain is usually about load under the metatarsal heads and how stiff the big toe is. Foot and calf work helps; so does the shoe.
forefoot.course: Improves over several weeks once the load pattern changes.
forefoot.helps: Calf strength, toe movement, and shoes that bend where your foot bends.

elbow-extension.name: Back of the elbow when you straighten under load
elbow-extension.explanation: The triceps insertion is loaded most at the end of straightening, so early work happens in mid-range.
elbow-extension.course: Tendon-type symptoms: expect several weeks of steady load.
elbow-extension.helps: Bent-elbow loading first, gradual straightening under load later.

biceps-tendon.name: Front of shoulder and elbow that ache together
biceps-tendon.explanation: The biceps tendon crosses both joints, so overhead load aggravates the shoulder and the elbow at once.
biceps-tendon.course: Usually settles in 4–8 weeks with graded loading.
biceps-tendon.helps: Reduce overhead volume, strengthen elbow flexion in mid-range.

wrist-load.name: Wrist pain when you push through it
wrist-load.explanation: Weight-bearing with the wrist bent back concentrates load on the small bones on the back of the wrist.
wrist-load.course: A few weeks of graded wrist loading, often with a brace for the aggravating activity.
wrist-load.helps: Keep the wrist straight when loading, build tolerance gradually.

hand-stiff.name: Stiff fingers and hand
hand-stiff.explanation: The hand loses movement quickly and regains it with repetition. Tendon gliding and gentle grip work keep things moving.
hand-stiff.course: Consistency matters more than intensity; several short sessions a day.
hand-stiff.helps: Move it often, avoid forcing a fist, warm the hand first.

chest-wall.name: Chest wall pain with movement or breathing
chest-wall.explanation: The joints where the ribs meet the breastbone are commonly tender and reproducible to touch. It is uncomfortable rather than dangerous — but chest symptoms still get checked.
chest-wall.course: Often settles in a few weeks with movement and breathing work.
chest-wall.helps: Deep breaths at your own pace, gentle opening, and an assessment if it is not clearly muscular.

tmj.name: Jaw joint that clicks, aches or locks
tmj.explanation: The jaw joint and the muscles of chewing are closely linked to neck posture and clenching. Position and habit changes do most of the work.
tmj.course: Varies; many settle with a few weeks of rest positions and stress management.
tmj.helps: Teeth apart, tongue on the roof of the mouth, soft diet for a week, and an assessment if it locks.

head-face-review.name: Head and face discomfort
head-face-review.explanation: Pain in the face, scalp or ear is usually not a muscle-joint problem that an exercise programme can fix. Neck-related headache is the exception, and we do treat that.
head-face-review.helps: If it came on suddenly and severely, or with visual or neurological change, seek care now.

front-of-neck-review.name: Front of the neck or throat
front-of-neck-review.explanation: Tenderness or a lump at the front of the neck needs a clinician rather than exercises. Neck movement from behind is often the actual source and we can treat that.
front-of-neck-review.course: Not an exercise-responsive pattern in most cases.
front-of-neck-review.helps: Get it assessed, especially with swallowing change, swelling or a persistent lump.

abdomen-review.name: Tummy-area discomfort
abdomen-review.explanation: Pain inside the abdomen is usually from organs rather than the wall. Muscle and nerve pain in the tummy wall does exist, and we can treat that after a clinician agrees.
abdomen-review.helps: New, severe, one-sided with a bulge, or with fever or bowel change: get seen.

olecranon-review.name: Tip of the elbow, swollen or warm
olecranon-review.explanation: The bursa at the tip of the elbow swells after leaning or a knock. Sometimes it becomes infected, which is not an exercise problem.
olecranon-review.course: Simple bursitis settles over weeks once the pressure is removed.
olecranon-review.helps: Stop leaning on it. If it is hot, red or you feel unwell, get seen today.
